step1_analysis.description: A wide-band interpolating amplifier used in a flash ADC. It features a multi-input differential pair with negative feedback to set the common-mode and perform signal averaging.

paper_reference.title: A 5-b 10-GSample/s A/D Converter for 10-Gb/s Optical Receivers

sky130_expected.reasoning: Paper reports power for the entire ADC. For a single amplifier stage in SKY130, power is determined by the tail currents chosen for proper DC biasing.

sky130_expected.calculation: First stage gain ~ 0.5 due to strong negative feedback. Second stage gain = gm * R = 2.7mA/V * 1k = 2.7. Total gain = 1.35 = 2.6 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Gain is lower in CMOS compared to SiGe bipolar due to lower gm. The 16dB in the paper likely refers to the entire THA or comparator.

sky130_expected.calculation: f_3dB = 1 / (2*pi*R*C). With R=1k and C~15fF, f_3dB ~ 10 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 130nm CMOS is slower than 100GHz SiGe BiCMOS, so bandwidth is expected to be slightly lower.

delay.description: Propagation delay from input to output

sky130_expected.calculation: t_delay ~ 0.69 * R * C per stage. For 2 stages, 2 * 0.69 * 1k * 15fF ~ 20 ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Delay is dominated by RC time constants. 25ps is reasonable for a low-gain wideband stage.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure power, gain, bandwidth, and delay of the interpolating amplifier.
